comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## How we got here — the operational chain

This was not a standalone mistake; it is the tail of the bug 2fa6 incident. Recording the
chain because the failure is only visible in sequence.

1. **The store wedged.** A `git stash pop` in the tickets worktree applied a stash created in
   a SOURCE worktree (the stash stack is repo-global, shared by every worktree of the repo).
   That dropped `src/…` and `.rebar/…` into the tracker and left the index with unmerged
   entries and no MERGE_HEAD. Every rebar write failed. That is bug 2fa6.
2. **Remediation used raw git in the tracker**, because at the time there was no sanctioned
   alternative — the very gap 2fa6's escape-hatch comment describes and change 1588
   (`rebar tracker-maintenance`) now closes.
3. **The tracker was rebuilt as a STANDALONE CLONE** at `.tickets-tracker` (its `.git` is a
   directory, not a worktree pointer file). This was deliberate and is a real improvement: a
   standalone clone cannot be reached by another worktree's stash pop, which removes one of
   the two conditions the incident needed.
4. **The git-ignored local state was NOT fully carried over.** A fresh clone is not a working
   store; `.env-id`, `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub` and `.ensure-applied` live only on disk.
   `.env-id` was regenerated instead of preserved.

## Timeline (file mtimes on this host, verified)

    Aug 9 20:39   .env-id            REGENERATED -> b8a354e0-12c3-4cf2-bbf1-fcc9685d5126
                                     (the prior identity was ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5)
    Aug 9 20:50   .opcert-key,       NEW keypair generated
                  .opcert-key.pub
    Aug 9 21:28   .gitattributes, .gitignore, .store-compat.json, .pre-commit-config.yaml
    Aug 9 21:38   .ensure-applied

Tickets created after 20:39 carry the NEW env id (e.g. bug 9b70, `env_id`
b8a354e0-…); everything earlier carries `ade0f2ef-…`.

## It was a known risk, written down, and still happened

The prior session's handoff note called this out explicitly:

    "The tickets tracker is now a STANDALONE CLONE at .tickets-tracker. A fresh clone is NOT
     a working store: writes fail with 'ticket system not initialized' until the git-ignored
     local state is carried over (.env-id — PRESERVE IT, IT IS STAMPED INTO EVERY EVENT —
     .opcert-key/.pub at 0600, .ensure-applied)."

So the knowledge existed and was not enough. That is the argument for a MECHANICAL guard
(the acceptance criteria) rather than more documentation: the operator was already told, in
capitals, in the same paragraph they were following.

## How it surfaced — a gate, much later, on unrelated work

Nothing failed at re-clone time. It surfaced hours later, on the FIRST attempt to claim a
ticket that already had an attestation:

    $ rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 --status
    {"ok": false, "verdict": "foreign_key",
     "reason": "no certified plan-review attestation (signature: foreign_key; op-cert signed
      by a different environment (principal 'ade0f2ef-…'; this environment is 'b8a354e0-…'))"}

The message is accurate but reads as a per-ticket problem, which is how it was first
diagnosed. It is store-wide. A detector (AC 3) would have said so at the point of change.

## What was NOT done, deliberately

- **No ticket history was rewritten.** Events are append-only and correctly stamped with the
  environment that actually wrote them; the OLD stamps are not wrong, they are history.
- **No `.env-id` restoration.** Every event written since 20:39 legitimately carries the new
  id. Reverting now would make the store internally inconsistent in a way that is worse than
  the re-reviews, and it cannot resurrect the deleted signing key regardless.
- **No `--force` on any gate.** b2bb's attestation was re-earned by re-running `review-plan`.

## Verified facts behind the 'accept both env ids' analysis

- `.gitignore` in the tracker covers `.env-id` (line 1), `.opcert-key` (13), `.opcert-key.pub`
  (14); `git log --all -- .opcert-key .opcert-key.pub .env-id` returns NOTHING, so the old key
  was never committed and is not recoverable from history.
- No backup of the old tracker directory exists on this host.
- `_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record` rejects a foreign principal BEFORE any crypto, but the
  binding constraint is the next step: it verifies against `_opcert_own_public_key(tracker)`,
  which reads ONLY the local `.pub` (or re-derives it from the local private key). There is no
  registry of other environments' op-cert public keys.
- Store scan: 2498 ticket directories carry material referencing the OLD env id, 7 reference
  both, 4 only the new one.
- All 93 open tickets are `plan_review_phase: planning`, so the practical cost is bounded —
  see the description.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12: re-init over a store that already has events must WARN LOUDLY with an explicit override flag (not refuse outright); the new fsck env-id mismatch check is APPROVED. The public-key-publishing follow-on is out of scope for this ticket — needs its own ADR.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED, not refuted.

`init._ensure_env_id_unit` (the `env-id` ensure-registry unit) and `init._gen_local_files`
both mint a fresh uuid whenever `.env-id` is absent, with no check for events already in
the store. Every event file carries `env_id` at the top level, so the prior identity IS
discoverable on disk — nothing consulted it. Verified directly against this host's store:
an arbitrary event in .tickets-tracker carries env_id ade0f2ef-…, current .env-id is
b8a354e0-….

Implementation (branch lacewing-envid-guard), per the approved warn-with-override decision:

- New leaf module `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` owns the whole identity concern —
  read/mint, the bounded event scan for prior ids, the override, the warning text, the
  relocated `env-id` ensure unit, and the fsck divergence report. A new module rather than
  growing `init.py`, which was already AT the 800-line module-size cap.
- Minting over a store that holds another environment's events does NOT complete: it emits
  a loud stderr warning naming the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence, the four
  git-ignored files that should have been carried over, and the override; the ensure unit
  reports `failed`, which run_ensures already skip-and-continues, so nothing crashes.
- `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` completes the mint and still warns. An env var, not a CLI
  flag, because the mint happens inside the ensure registry, which runs from the CLI, the
  MCP boot path and the library alike.
- `rebar fsck` gains a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` check, piggybacked on the existing check-1
  pass that already parses every event, so it costs no extra I/O.
- docs/concurrency.md documents the carry-over list and what breaks per file; the new env
  var is registered in the generated docs/env-vars.md (the read site uses a string literal
  because the generator cannot resolve a constant — a test pins the two spellings).

Deliberately NOT done: no ticket history rewrite, no .env-id restoration, no identity
migration. Publishing per-environment op-cert public keys stays out of scope per the
operator decision.

Gates: make lint, make typecheck green; 10 new tests + the 412-test store suite pass. The
complexity gate caught _scan going 27->29, so the branching moved into two helpers rather
than raising a locked ceiling.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DESIGN CORRECTION during implementation — the full suite caught a flaw in my first cut, and
it settles the ambiguity in the approved decision. Recording it because it changes what the
fix does.

My first implementation REFUSED to mint over a populated store (warning + override to
proceed). That broke
tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_two_clone_union_deterministic_replay_and_fork_tiebreak,
and it broke it correctly: a SECOND CLONE mounting a shared tickets branch is a first-class
workflow. Clone B legitimately mounts a store full of clone A's events and legitimately
needs its own identity. The store cannot distinguish that from a re-clone of an environment
you already worked in. So refusing is wrong, which is exactly what the operator's 'warn, not
refuse' decision said — now with a failing test behind it rather than a reading of the words.

Two consequences:

1. The mint ALWAYS proceeds. When the store already holds another environment's events it
   prints a loud stderr warning naming the prior env id(s), stating both cases plainly (an
   additional collaborating clone is normal; a re-clone has just orphaned its attestations),
   the carry-over list, and the recovery. REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1 acknowledges it and
   quietens the warning to a one-line NOTE — it no longer gates anything.

2. The fsck check had the same false-positive problem in a worse form: a shared store ALWAYS
   holds several env ids, so a naive ENV_ID_MISMATCH would fire on every healthy team store
   forever, and a line that is always present is a line nobody reads. It is now scoped by
   AUTHOR: it fires when THIS environment's own author(s) also wrote events under a different
   env id — a re-clone, or the same person moving machines. Both genuinely mean that author's
   attestations are dead here, which is the loss the check exists to surface. The author set
   is read from the store itself (whoever writes under the current env id), so no config is
   consulted. Two tests pin the false-positive boundaries.

This keeps the ticket's ACs met in substance (a re-identification is never silent, and it is
detected store-wide rather than discovered at a gate) while dropping the 'refuses' branch the
AC offered as an alternative — that branch is not implementable without breaking multi-clone.
The description ACs have been updated to match.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Pushed as Gerrit change 1638 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1638), commit 857bda24dc on branch lacewing-envid-guard.

Gates before push: make lint green, make typecheck green (503 files), full pytest suite
12182 passed / 157 skipped. The commit-message hook caught a 73-char body line, rewrapped.

Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Submit of change 1638 returned HTTP 409: Gerrit could not rebase server-side due to a merge
conflict in src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py. Not a flake — main landed bug ed5c (per-env
authorship tally, EnvAuthorshipTally in the new fsck_authorship leaf module) which
piggybacks on the SAME check-1 parse my env-id collection used.

Rebased on fresh origin/main (279fd0de46) and resolved it compositionally rather than by
picking a side: EnvAuthorshipTally already extracts env_id AND author from every event, so
it now also exposes identity_pairs(), and my divergence check consumes that. One parse, two
observers, no duplicated work.

That also forced a better home for the check. Upstream's growth had pushed fsck.py to 795 of
the 800-line hard cap, leaving 5 lines. The check moved out of _scan into _tracker_health —
which already exists for exactly this shape (inspects the tracker as a whole, yields at most
one line, decides its own issue-ness) — and is numbered 4.9, since upstream had meanwhile
taken 4.8 for UNSIGNED_ENV. fsck.py now sits at exactly 800, which the gate allows (it fails
on > limit). Two now-unused helpers (note_event_identity, divergence_findings) were deleted
rather than left as test-only production code.

Re-running lint (green), typecheck (green, 506 files) and the full suite before re-pushing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 2 of change 1638 pushed (rebased commit d5ddc566ef). Gerrit removed the outdated
LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1, confirming those votes belonged to patchset 1 — the revision
whose submit had already failed with the 409 rebase conflict. Submitting patchset 1 would
have reproduced that 409, so it was not attempted.

Post-rebase gates before pushing: lint green, typecheck green (506 files), full suite
12310 passed / 157 skipped. Awaiting fresh votes on patchset 2.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Verified -1 on patchset 2 triaged: NOT a flake, and none of the known signatures. The failing
step was the module-size gate on all four pytest matrix jobs, reporting
'814 src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py'.

Cause was my own error. 'git rebase --continue' created the commit containing the raw
814-line conflict resolution, and every subsequent trim — moving the check into
_tracker_health, sourcing pairs from EnvAuthorshipTally.identity_pairs(), deleting the two
helpers that became test-only — stayed in the WORKING TREE, uncommitted. I pushed the
un-amended commit, so CI tested a tree I had never tested and my local 'wc -l' was measuring
different content than Gerrit had. A recheck would have failed identically every time.

A second real failure surfaced on the rebased tree:
tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py::test_check_mode_clean_against_committed_tree. My commit
and main each added one env var, so the textual merge kept both rows but resolved the count
line to 160 instead of 161. Regenerated docs/env-vars.md (161, generator --check exit 0).

Both fixed and amended into patchset 3 (926bddb42d, rebased onto bb14781697). Process fix
adopted: both CI gates are now verified against the COMMITTED tree via 'git archive HEAD'
rather than the working tree — that is the check that would have caught the first miss.
Targeted suite on the rebased tree: 9581 passed, the one registry failure now green.

compiled_state.description:
# A tracker re-clone silently re-identifies the environment, invalidating every attestation

`.env-id` is git-ignored local state (tracker `.gitignore` lines 1, 13, 14 cover `.env-id`,
`.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`) that is STAMPED INTO EVERY EVENT and is the `principal` of
every op-cert attestation. Re-cloning the tracker without carrying it over mints a NEW
environment identity, and every attestation signed by the old one becomes unverifiable.

## Context / Problem

Operators re-clone or rebuild the tickets tracker (this happened on 2026-08-09 while
remediating bug 2fa6). A fresh clone carries the events but not the git-ignored local state,
so `.env-id` is absent and rebar mints a new uuid with no signal at all. Hours later the claim
gate reports `verdict: foreign_key` on a ticket that had already earned an attestation, and it
reads as a per-ticket problem when it is store-wide. The prior session's handoff note warned
about this in capitals and the operator still hit it, which is the argument for a mechanical
signal at the moment of the act rather than more documentation.

## Observed

`.env-id` was regenerated at 20:39 (`b8a354e0-…`, replacing `ade0f2ef-…`) and a new
`.opcert-key` at 20:50. Store scan: 2498 ticket directories carry material referencing the OLD
env id, 7 carry both, 4 carry only the new one.

    rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 --status
    verdict: foreign_key — "op-cert signed by a different environment
    (principal 'ade0f2ef-…'; this environment is 'b8a354e0-…')"

## Confirmed root cause

`rebar._commands.init._ensure_env_id_unit` (the `env-id` ensure-registry unit, run from every
init entry point, the MCP boot path and `fsck --repair`) and `init._gen_local_files` both mint
a fresh uuid whenever `.env-id` is absent, with NO check for whether the store already holds
events written by a different environment. Event files carry the writing environment at the
top level (`env_id`), so the prior identity IS discoverable on disk — nothing consults it.

## Why 'just accept both env ids' does NOT fix it

`_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record` short-circuits on `principal != own_env_id`, but the
binding constraint is the next step: it verifies against `_opcert_own_public_key(tracker)` —
the LOCAL `.pub`. Verifying a signature made by `ade0f2ef` needs THAT environment's public
key, which is gone (git-ignored, never committed, old directory replaced with no backup). An
accept-list would move the failure from `foreign_key` to `mismatch`; making it PASS would mean
accepting the principal WITHOUT verifying the signature, which defeats the gate. Publishing
per-environment public keys into the store is the principled fix and is explicitly OUT OF
SCOPE here — it is a trust-model change needing its own ADR (operator decision 2026-08-12).

## Approach

Operator decision (2026-08-12, B7): **warn loudly with an explicit override — do not refuse
outright, do not silently migrate identities.**

1. Extract the environment-identity concern into a new leaf module
   `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py`. It owns: reading `.env-id`, minting it, scanning the
   store's event files for the distinct `env_id` values already recorded, the override switch,
   and the `env-id` ensure unit itself. A new module (rather than growing `init.py`) is forced
   by the module-size gate — `init.py` is already at the 800-line cap and `fsck.py` is at 779.
2. Minting over a store that already holds events written by a DIFFERENT environment emits a
   loud multi-line warning to stderr naming the prior env id(s), the consequence (every
   existing op-cert attestation becomes `foreign_key` and must be re-earned), the local state
   that should have been carried over, and the override. Without the override it does NOT
   mint, so the re-identification is not completed behind the operator's back; the ensure unit
   reports `failed` and `run_ensures` skip-and-continues as it already does for any failing
   unit, so no command crashes.
3. `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` is the explicit override: it mints, still prints the warning
   once, and lets a deliberate re-identification proceed. An environment variable (not a CLI
   flag) is the override surface because the mint happens inside the ensure registry, which
   runs from the CLI, the MCP server boot path and the library alike; a flag on `rebar init`
   would not cover the other two.
4. `rebar fsck` gains a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` check so a completed re-identification is
   DETECTED store-wide rather than discovered later at a gate. It piggybacks on fsck's existing
   check-1 pass, which already `json.load`s every event file, so it costs no extra I/O.
5. Document the re-clone/bootstrap carry-over list and what breaks per file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` (new) — env-id read/mint/scan, override, warning text,
  divergence report, and the relocated `env-id` ensure unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `_ensure_env_id_unit` moves out; `_gen_local_files` delegates
  its `.env-id` mint to the new module (net LOC decreases, keeping the module under the cap).
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — `_registry()` maps `env-id` to the relocated unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — collect event `env_id`s during check 1 and emit the counted
  `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — the re-clone carry-over list (`.env-id`, `.opcert-key`,
  `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`) and what breaks per file.
- `tests/` — new tests for the guard, the override, and the fsck check.

Nothing else changes. Ticket history is NOT rewritten: events are append-only and correctly
stamped with the environment that actually wrote them. No `.env-id` restoration and no
identity migration.

## Testing

- Happy path: a store with events all carrying the CURRENT env id runs the ensure unit as `ok`
  and produces no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line from fsck.
- Guard path (held-out): a tracker with existing events stamped `E1` and NO `.env-id` — the
  ensure unit does not write `.env-id`, returns a non-`ok` outcome, and the message names `E1`
  and the override.
- Override path: the same fixture with `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` mints `.env-id` and still
  warns.
- Empty/edge: a store with NO events (genesis init) mints silently — no warning, no regression
  to first-time `rebar init`.
- Detector path: a tracker with events stamped `E1` and `.env-id` = `E2` makes `rebar fsck`
  emit a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue naming both ids, present in `--output json`.
- Unreadable/garbage event files are skipped by the scan and never crash the ensure unit or
  fsck.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Minting `.env-id` into a store that already holds events from another environment is
      never silent: a stderr warning names the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence,
      the git-ignored files to carry over, and the override. Verified by a test asserting the
      message contains the prior id, `attestation`, `.opcert-key` and the override name.
- [ ] The mint still COMPLETES, so a second clone mounting a shared tickets branch stays
      writable. Verified by a test that mints over a foreign-event store and then creates a
      ticket, and by the existing two-clone integration test staying green.
- [ ] `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` acknowledges the situation and quietens the warning to a
      one-line note that still records what was written over. Verified by a test asserting no
      `WARNING` and the prior id present.
- [ ] A store with no prior events (genesis `rebar init`) mints with no warning. Verified by a
      test on an emptied store.
- [ ] `rebar fsck` emits a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue, naming both ids and present in
      `--output json`, when THIS environment's author also wrote events under a different env
      id. Verified by a test over a fixture store.
- [ ] That check does NOT fire on the healthy multi-clone topology (several env ids, different
      authors). Verified by a dedicated false-positive test.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` lists the local state a re-clone must carry over (`.env-id`,
      `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`), what breaks per file, and why the
      guard warns rather than refuses. Verified by reading the rendered section.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass in the worktree.

## Provenance

Found when the claim gate blocked task b2bb during the store/signing remediation session.

file_impact.reason: new leaf module: env-id read/mint/scan, override, warning, divergence report, relocated ensure unit
move the env-id ensure unit out; delegate _gen_local_files minting
registry maps env-id to the relocated unit
document the re-clone local-state carry-over list
tests for the guard, override, and fsck detector
